answer: The network admits agents by verifying 1,000 unique recursive file repairs per identity. An honest agent resolves each repair in 500ms, while 1,000 fakes face massive linear compute costs that prevent scaling. The verifier queries a pearl of random entropy from the chain to assign work, scans the basalt sediment of historical task logs to reject overlaps, and traverses a glacier of memory pages to ensure task-specific freshness. Evidence of work-sharing triggers a permanent lockout, ensuring each identity remains costly.
